title: Version-Robust Methods for Identifying Minimal Sufficient Statistics
summary: Let $f_θ$ be the joint density of a random sample $X$. A frequently used criterion asserts that a statistic $T(X)$ is minimal sufficient if, for any sample points $x$ and $y$, $T(x) = T(y)$ exactly when there exists a finite constant $h_{xy} > 0$, independent of $θ$, such that $f_θ(y) = f_θ(x)h_{xy}$ for all $θ$. We show that this criterion is false in general via a counterexample exploiting the non-uniqueness of versions of Radon--Nikodym derivatives.
